methodology.description: Public draft-helper PPR redraft board. Player value and market cost are intentionally kept separate. Rankings blend broad expert consensus, current projections, recent independent expert boards and material preseason/news context; ADP is treated as price rather than player quality. League scoring, roster construction, draft slot, drafted players, positional scarcity and next-pick pressure are applied by the client recommendation engine.
rankingInputs: FantasyPros 2026 PPR consensus and positional consensus checked Aug. 31
ESPN Field Yates PPR Top 160 updated Aug. 31 plus ESPN current depth charts and cutdown tracker
RotoWire current 2026 PPR top-300 and recent expert-consensus boards checked Aug. 31
Rotoworld/NBC Sports Top 200 published Aug. 26 and current player-news feed checked Aug. 31
Yahoo Sports injury/ADP analysis and CBS/PFF/FantasyPros preseason coverage checked through Aug. 31
methodology.marketInput: Current PPR ADP remains a separate market-price input, cross-checked across FantasyPros, Yahoo/CBS and other platform-market references. ADP is not used as a substitute for player value; large gaps remain when injury risk, role uncertainty or expert disagreement justifies them.
newsInputs: Christian McCaffrey moves from No. 7 to No. 6. ESPN has him No. 3, RotoWire No. 6 and Rotoworld No. 6, so the prior rank was a little too conservative while still preserving a broad injury-risk range.
De'Von Achane moves from No. 11 to No. 9. ESPN now has him No. 8 and RotoWire No. 7, while Rotoworld remains more conservative around No. 13. The board moves upward without erasing that disagreement.

Kenneth Walker III moves from No. 20 to No. 17. ESPN ranks him No. 15, Rotoworld No. 18 and current injury reporting says the recent foot/ankle concern is not expected to alter his normal workload materially.
Derrick Henry moves from No. 21 to No. 16. ESPN has him No. 11, Rotoworld No. 17 and RotoWire remains somewhat lower, producing a center clearly above the prior No. 21 value.

Jeremiyah Love is added at No. 24. ESPN has him No. 20 and a current RotoWire top-300 has him No. 16, while other recent RotoWire consensus work has been much lower around the low 30s. His ankle is expected to allow Week 1 availability, but the offensive environment and wide expert split keep confidence moderate.

Ashton Jeanty moves from No. 28 to No. 23. Injury analysis increasingly describes the ankle issue as short-term, and ESPN now has him No. 23 while RotoWire is much more aggressive. Rotoworld remains near No. 29, so the disagreement range stays intentionally wide.
Rashee Rice moves from No. 25 to No. 21 and Trey McBride from No. 22 to No. 20 as fresh ESPN ranks (No. 19 and No. 18 respectively) pull their cross-source centers upward.
Final 53-man roster moves created several depth-chart changes around the league, but none justified a larger top-30 move than the changes above.
methodology.notes: Expert disagreement is preserved with expertHigh/expertLow ranges; unresolved injuries, discipline risk and genuine model disagreement can intentionally widen those ranges. Confidence reflects agreement plus news certainty, not ceiling. This file is used only by smhillis/sleeper-draft-helper-public and must not be copied into or used to modify Scott's personal Sleeper Draft Assistant.

players.name: Puka Nacua
players.news: Still elite by talent and projection, but the board keeps a wider downside band for the recent soft-tissue concern and unresolved discipline uncertainty.

players.name: Christian McCaffrey
players.news: Moves up one spot. ESPN has him No. 3 and both RotoWire and Rotoworld are around No. 6; age and recent tightness keep the downside band wider than the rank alone implies.

players.name: De'Von Achane
players.news: Moves from No. 11 to No. 9. ESPN is No. 8 and RotoWire No. 7, while Rotoworld remains closer to No. 13. The higher value rank does not erase the durability and offensive-environment disagreement.

players.name: Derrick Henry
players.news: Moves from No. 21 to No. 16. ESPN is No. 11 and Rotoworld No. 17; age-driven skepticism remains valid, but the prior rank sat below the current cross-source center.

players.name: Kenneth Walker III
players.news: Moves from No. 20 to No. 17. ESPN is No. 15 and Rotoworld No. 18, while current injury reporting says the recent foot issue should not materially alter his normal draft value.

players.name: Trey McBride
players.news: Moves from No. 22 to No. 20 after ESPN's Aug. 31 board placed him No. 18; other sources remain lower, so the move is modest rather than theatrical.

players.name: Rashee Rice
players.news: Moves from No. 25 to No. 21. ESPN is No. 19 and some projection-driven boards are similarly bullish, while other expert boards remain far lower, leaving one of the widest disagreement ranges in the top 30.

players.name: Ashton Jeanty
players.news: Moves from No. 28 to No. 23 as the ankle outlook improves. ESPN now has him No. 23 and RotoWire is substantially more aggressive, while Rotoworld remains near No. 29. Market price is still richer than this value rank.

players.name: Jeremiyah Love
players.news: Added to the centralized board. ESPN has him No. 20 and one current RotoWire projection board No. 16, but other recent expert consensus has him in the low 30s. Week 1 availability looks plausible; offensive-environment risk keeps the range wide.

players.name: Nico Collins
players.news: Drops from No. 23 to No. 28 as fresh ESPN work has him No. 39 while Rotoworld and RotoWire remain much higher. The rank moves down but the wide disagreement is explicitly preserved.
